subject: Pilot MAP & SLA ask — Atlas x Redwood
messages:
From: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@atlasanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@atlasanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot MAP & SLA ask — Atlas x Redwood

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Atlas is ready to move from exploration to a scoped pilot, and procurement asked me to put the proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and our key SLA asks in writing so we can align on commercial milestones. High level: we want a 30-day evaluation, then a 1-month pilot (proof-of-concept), followed by a ramp to 50k requests/day within 90 days of pilot completion.

What we need from Redwood to commit:
- Pricing schedule that maps discounts to committed monthly spend and ramp milestones.
- A MAP with owner, milestone dates, and acceptance criteria.
- SLOs for latency (95th pct): embeddings <= 120ms, chat generation <= 300ms, measured per-region in-prod.
- Service credit language or commercial concession if SLOs are missed in two consecutive months.

I attached a short MAP draft showing our proposed milestones and acceptance tests (Atlas_MAP_v1.pdf). Procurement will review commercial language once engineering and CS agree on the acceptance criteria and SLO measurement approach.

Can Redwood provide a proposal that ties a preliminary discount to the initial commit (we're targeting $40k/mo at start, scaling to $150k/mo within 12 months) and clarifies how SLO concessions or credits are triggered? Also please confirm who from Redwood will own the MAP and the technical evaluation.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Emma Thomas
Head of Platform
Atlas Analytics
[Attachment: Atlas_MAP_v1.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@atlasanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@atlasanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & SLA ask — Atlas x Redwood

Emma — appreciate the clear MAP. We can absolutely work this as a milestone-driven plan. High-level response below; attaching a proposed MAP that maps discounts to ramp (Redwood_Proposed_MAP.pdf) and a preliminary quote (Quote-Atlas-2026-03.pdf).

Proposed commercial framework (summary):
- Initial pilot pricing: 20% off list for first 3 months in exchange for a 3-month minimum pilot commit ($40k/mo).
- Ramp milestones: additional 10% discount at $75k/mo and 30% total at $150k/mo sustained for 3 months.
- If Atlas hits ramp milestones within the mutually-agreed dates in the MAP, Redwood will provide a credit equal to one month of the discount differential as a sign-on concession.

SLOs and concessions:
- Redwood will commit to 95th-pctl latency targets by region for the first 6 months: embeddings <= 120ms, chat gen <= 300ms.
- If SLOs are missed for two consecutive billing months, we propose a capped commercial concession (bill credit) up to 15% of that month's invoice, not to exceed credits over the first 6 months.
- We want to avoid uncapped liability — legal will propose precise language.

Next steps:
1) I'll loop in Legal to draft SLO language for the contract.
2) Redwood CS (Logan) will propose a joint evaluation plan and baseline test harness to measure latency in each region.
3) Once we agree on MAP milestones and acceptance criteria, I'll get procurement-friendly terms for signature.

Call me Thurs if you want to review the MAP walk-through (30m).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_MAP.pdf][Attachment: Quote-Atlas-2026-03.pdf]

From: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@atlasanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & SLA ask — Atlas x Redwood

Thanks Marissa — that framework makes sense. A couple of clarifications from engineering: how will latency be measured for model variants (we may use an embeddings-only flow for search and a different model for chat surfaces)? We need per-API-endpoint SLOs and an agreed measurement harness (real in-prod traffic or a synthetic runner).

Also procurement asked that any credit/discount triggers be tied to customer-observed metrics (we want a transparent telemetry window). If legal will propose credit caps and measurement rules, procurement will accept that; they'd just like to see the instrumentation plan.

I've attached a slightly updated MAP with our suggested acceptance tests and ramp dates.

— Emma
[Attachment: Atlas_MAP_v1.pdf (updated)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@atlasanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@atlasanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & SLA ask — Atlas x Redwood

Emma / Marissa — looping in Legal. High level thoughts on SLA language and commercial concessions: 

1) Measurement window and telemetry
- We need to codify the measurement method: 95th pctl calculated on production traffic aggregated daily then averaged across the billing month per-region. We'll provide access to aggregated telemetry dashboards and a downloadable CSV for audit.

2) Trigger and remedy
- Propose that a remediation threshold is reached when the 95th-pctl for a region exceeds the SLO for two consecutive billing months. Remedy = one-time bill credit applied to the next invoice, capped at 15% of that month's invoice.

3) Liability, exclusions, and force majeure
- Exclude incidents caused by customer misconfiguration, on-prem network issues, and third-party infra outages. Liability limited to aggregated credits as above; no additional indemnity tied to latency.

4) Acceptance tests / MAP alignment
- We should reference the MAP milestones in the contract and include a jointly-signed evaluation-plan as an exhibit. That makes ramp-to-discount milestones objective.

I attached a draft SLA for review (SLA-draft.docx) and Redwood's SOC2 attestation for procurement. Happy to redline.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA-draft.docx][Attachment: SOC2-Attestation.pdf]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@atlasanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & SLA ask — Atlas x Redwood

Emma — Logan from CS here. Quick note on instrumentation and the joint evaluation plan:

- Redwood will provide a scripted evaluation harness (see evaluation-plan.md in Drive) that can run against Atlas staging and then a controlled canary in production. The harness captures per-request timing (client->edge, edge->model, model decode).
- We propose a two-phase measurement: Phase A = staging baseline (synthetic runner), Phase B = 30-day production canary with sampling (1% of traffic or up to configured qps) agreed in the MAP.
- For model variants: each API endpoint and model variant will have its own acceptance tests. Ramp milestones tied to specific endpoints (search embeddings vs chat).

I'll schedule a 60-min joint runbook session where we walk through the harness, sample data schema, and dashboard access. That session will also define how we calculate the 95th pctl (per-region, per-endpoint).

Link to the evaluation plan and sample dashboards: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/atlas-eval-plan

— Logan Wright
Customer Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evaluation-plan.md]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@atlasanalytics.com>, procurement <procurement@atlasanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & SLA ask — Atlas x Redwood

Emma — great sync across teams this week. Summary and next steps (approved by Legal & CS):

Summary of commercial & SLO concessions:
- MAP milestones: evaluation (30d) -> pilot (30d) -> ramp to 50k req/day within 90d of pilot completion. Owners: Atlas (Emma) / Redwood (Marissa).
- Pricing: 20% off list during 3-month pilot (minimum $40k/mo) with staged discounts tied to ramp (see attached Quote-Atlas-2026-03.pdf).
- SLOs: Redwood commits to 95th-pctl latency <= 120ms (embeddings) and <= 300ms (chat gen) per-region for the first 6 months after go-live.
- Remedy: If SLOs are missed for two consecutive billing months, Redwood will issue a one-time bill credit up to 15% of that month's invoice. Credits are capped and exclude customer-caused issues.

Contract/close timeline:
1) Legal will incorporate SLA language and MAP as an exhibit this week (Karthik).
2) Procurement review and redlines (Atlas) — target completion by 2026-03-12.
3) Signature and initial invoice by 2026-03-19.
4) Joint evaluation runbook session w/ CS to set baseline (Logan) within 3 business days of signature.

If this aligns, please reply with a one-line approval from procurement (procurement@atlasanalytics.com) and we'll push the contract to DocuSign. I've attached the final MAP and the quote for signatures.

Thanks — excited to get started.

— Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
